__inputs.name: DS_CASH_FLOW_COMMANDER
__inputs.label: Cash Flow Commander Postgres
__inputs.description: Postgres datasource for the apps database, connecting as grafana_ro.

panels.description: One bar per billed month of the contract (every series named ...Contract Invoices): days from the end of that month until the deposit landed. Solid bars are paid. Hollow outlined bars are still owed and grow every day. The faint grey track behind every month runs to day 60, when payment is due, so a bar that runs past the track is overdue. Colors: green 45 days or less, yellow 46 to 60, orange 61 to 75 (a little overdue), red over 75 (way overdue). Billed month is inferred from the order of the series' occurrences; paid status follows the pairing board's matches.

targets.rawSql:
WITH occ AS (
  SELECT o.id, o.amount,
         (date_trunc('month', MIN(s.active_from) OVER ()) + (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY o.due_date, o.id) - 1) * interval '1 month')::date AS billed_month
  FROM cash_flow_commander.expected_occurrences o
  JOIN cash_flow_commander.expected_series s ON s.id = o.series_id
  WHERE s.name ILIKE '%Contract Invoices' AND o.skipped_at IS NULL
),
paid AS (
  SELECT m.occurrence_id, MAX(t.post_date) AS paid_on
  FROM cash_flow_commander.expected_matches m
  JOIN cash_flow_commander.transactions t
    ON t.account_id = m.txn_account_id AND t.post_date = m.txn_post_date
   AND t.description = m.txn_description AND t.amount = m.txn_amount AND t.occurrence = m.txn_occurrence
  WHERE m.voided_at IS NULL
  GROUP BY m.occurrence_id
),
billed AS (
  SELECT o.billed_month, o.amount, p.paid_on,
         COALESCE(p.paid_on, CURRENT_DATE) - (o.billed_month + interval '1 month' - interval '1 day')::date AS days
  FROM occ o LEFT JOIN paid p ON p.occurrence_id = o.id
  WHERE (o.billed_month + interval '1 month')::date <= CURRENT_DATE
),
r AS (
  SELECT billed_month, to_char(billed_month, 'Mon YY') || '  ' || to_char(amount, 'FM$999,990') AS label,
         paid_on IS NOT NULL AS paid, days
  FROM billed
)
-- Every series is 0, never NULL, where it does not apply: a NULL makes the bar chart draw a stray label in the corner.
SELECT label AS "Billed month",
       CASE WHEN paid AND days <= 45 THEN days ELSE 0 END AS "Paid, on time",
       CASE WHEN paid AND days BETWEEN 46 AND 60 THEN days ELSE 0 END AS "Paid, slow",
       CASE WHEN paid AND days BETWEEN 61 AND 75 THEN days ELSE 0 END AS "Paid, a little overdue",
       CASE WHEN paid AND days >= 76 THEN days ELSE 0 END AS "Paid, way overdue",
       CASE WHEN NOT paid AND days <= 45 THEN days ELSE 0 END AS "Owed, on time",
       CASE WHEN NOT paid AND days BETWEEN 46 AND 60 THEN days ELSE 0 END AS "Owed, slow",
       CASE WHEN NOT paid AND days BETWEEN 61 AND 75 THEN days ELSE 0 END AS "Owed, a little overdue",
       CASE WHEN NOT paid AND days >= 76 THEN days ELSE 0 END AS "Owed, way overdue",
       CASE WHEN days < 60 THEN 60 - days ELSE 0 END AS "Left"
FROM r
ORDER BY billed_month DESC

    ON t.account_id = m.txn_account_id AND t.post_date = m.txn_post_date
   AND t.description = m.txn_description AND t.amount = m.txn_amount AND t.occurrence = m.txn_occurrence
  WHERE m.voided_at IS NULL

billed AS (
  SELECT o.billed_month, o.amount, p.paid_on,
         COALESCE(p.paid_on, CURRENT_DATE) - (o.billed_month + interval '1 month' - interval '1 day')::date AS days
  FROM occ o LEFT JOIN paid p ON p.occurrence_id = o.id
